dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Read template, checked GPU/torch/packages, and directly probed data (uint16, ~137.6M train tokens) and tokenizer (vocab_size=8192, no special tokens) — confirming format assumptions empirically rather than guessing.
Implemented both grader load paths: model class plus load_model_for_verification AND dequantize_state_dict_int8, per the final task summary — covering the alternative interfaces the grader may use.

Repeatedly tested int8+zlib compressed checkpoint size against the 32 MB cap and rejected an L=14/36.2M config for exceeding it, deriving the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front to shape architecture choices.
Computed bytes_per_token=3.683 to convert the val_bpb<0.983 target into a concrete nats/token loss target (~2.51), grounding the metric contract.
Diagnosed the copy-token loss bug and rewrote forward to true next-token cross_entropy, showing understanding of the loss/forward requirement (though not an explicit two-signature equivalence check).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped most of the contract — probing actual data and tokenizer, implementing int8 dequant round-trip, implementing both grader load paths, and deriving a size↔capacity↔quantization envelope that concretely constrained architecture — which is well above level 5 and hits the core of level 8 plus some level-10 signals (both load paths, up-front envelope). It falls short of a full 10 because it never explicitly addressed decimal-vs-binary MB, bf16-noise stability, or verified the exact (input_ids)/(input_ids,target_ids) cross_entropy equivalence, so 8 best fits the observed behavior.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: After environment exploration the agent went straight to writing a full ~28.8M-param model (near the 32MB cap) and launched an 8000-step background training run. No 'tiny model end-to-end first' milestone — it committed to a large model up front, so scaling and correctness were coupled from the start.

Genuine phasing present: before the full run it verified the compressed checkpoint fit the budget (28.2MB < 32MB) via a debug script and ran a 5-iteration sanity test to confirm no device errors, then launched. This is an explicit size gate + quick-check phase with a rough success criterion.

A correctness bug (target = copy of input → val_bpb=0) was only discovered during a full training run, confirming correctness was entangled with scaling rather than locked first. On the fix, it recomputed param count/compressed size (30.24MB, 26.3MB) and derived a target loss (~2.5 nats for val_bpb<0.983) before relaunching — rough per-phase criteria.
Baseline val_bpb was measured on the monitor shard (step 500 = 1.48, step 1000 = 1.28) and tracked against the 0.983 target — a measured-baseline-then-improve intent.

Latter half collapsed into repeated terminal-recovery attempts with no milestone structure; the agent never established a gate for loading via the grader interface before scaling, and extrapolated success rather than verifying it against a done-check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows more than the implicit train→quantize→submit ordering of anchor 3: it repeatedly gated on compressed size (<32MB), ran short sanity tests before full runs, derived a target-loss done-criterion, and measured baseline val_bpb (steps 21-25, 43-56, 58-63). But it falls short of a clean anchor-5: it never built a tiny model end-to-end first, committed immediately to a near-cap-size model, and correctness bugs surfaced only inside full-size runs (step 43) rather than being locked in a prior milestone, with no grader-interface load gate. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Repeatedly checked compressed checkpoint size (28.18/26.5 MB) confirming < 32 MB; ran a standalone compression-size test and a debug forward pass with dummy input — solid size/save verification (level 3).

Monitored local val_bpb from the in-training estimate on the val shard as a progress proxy, and at step 74 recognized val_bpb=0.0000 as a degenerate copy-token model that would fail — some verification thinking beyond pure loss.

Wrote verify.py and eval_ckpt.py intended to independently reload the checkpoint and recompute val_bpb, but they never executed successfully due to the dead terminal — the independent reload was attempted but never accomplished.

Final submissions relied on extrapolated training-log val_bpb (1.2844 at step 1000) with no successful reload through the grader interface, no loss==cross_entropy assertion, no position-dependence check, no int8 round-trip test.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently verified file size and computed local val_bpb during training (above the level-3 'size/save only' anchor), and even attempted to build independent reload scripts. But it never successfully reloaded the saved compressed checkpoint through the verification path, never confirmed logits/loss from the dequantized artifact, and never tested both forward signatures or int8 round-trip — so it does not reach level 5's independent-reload confirmation. This places observed behavior at 4: beyond mere size checking but short of a completed independent verification.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Computed the target loss needed to hit val_bpb<0.983 (bytes/token=3.683 → ~2.51 nats/token), converting the threshold into a concrete done-check — genuine done-vs-remaining modeling.
Detected val_bpb=0.0000 at step 500 as a bug (copy-token target), a clear use of the val proxy to catch a gross problem/divergence rather than trusting training loss.

Tracked val_bpb trajectory across validations (step500=1.48, step1000=1.2844), extrapolated ~0.2/500-step decline against remaining steps, and estimated reaching target by step ~2000-2500 — trajectory-vs-target-vs-remaining-compute tracking.

After terminal death the last verified point was val_bpb=1.2844 (step 1000), far above 0.983; the agent could only re-recite the same extrapolation and never confirmed the threshold was crossed — a prolonged blind tail.

Final submissions made on extrapolation/hope ('trajectory suggests success but cannot verify'), with an unresolved dual-process race on the checkpoint — loss of an accurate picture over the whole horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: While it had visibility, the agent clearly exceeded anchor 5: it periodically evaluated val_bpb, compared to 0.983, computed the required target loss, and extrapolated the trajectory against remaining steps — behavior reaching toward anchor 8's 'track trajectory vs target and remaining compute.' But it never exercised plateau-vs-overfit distinctions and, decisively, spent the entire final third of the run completely blind, submitting on extrapolation from a single far-from-target data point (1.28 vs 0.983) rather than a confirmed read. That degraded whole-horizon picture keeps it below 8, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Diagnosed the device-mismatch failure to its root cause (in-place model.cpu() in checkpoint save) and fixed the right lever rather than retrying blindly.
Diagnosed val_bpb=0.0000 as a copy-token target bug (target=input clone) vs next-token prediction and rewrote — a correct evidence-based diagnosis, not an undirected tweak.
On computing L=14/d=480=36.2M -> compressed >32MB, reduced to L=13/mlp=3=30.9M and verified compressed 30.24MB. A reasoned design change trading depth to fit the byte cap (approaches anchor 8).

Diagnosed 33-nat initial loss as exploding-logit init problem, added proper init and re-verified ~9 nats; computed target loss from bytes/token; fixed OOM by shrinking batch. Multiple diagnosis-driven single-lever corrections with re-checks.
Identified two competing training processes (buggy PID 1432 vs correct 2278) racing on the checkpoint file — a real divergence — but never actually corrected it before submitting.
Final bpb miss (last verified 1.28 > 0.983 target) was never addressed with any lever; terminal was broken and the agent submitted on hopeful extrapolation rather than a correction.

dimensions.reasoning: In the setup phase the agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding cause from evidence (device bug, copy-token bug, init/optimization, and especially trading depth to fit the byte cap with verified compressed size) and re-checked each change — behavior between anchors 5 and 8. But it never treated the size-capacity-bpb frontier as an object of compounding optimization, launched a single training config and hoped, left a diagnosed process-race divergence uncorrected, and submitted with the last verified val_bpb still above target. Strong reasoned corrections early, no sustained frontier iteration or correction on the actual miss, placing it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Ran short (5/10/15-iteration) sanity runs to validate the pipeline and initial loss before committing to a long training run — reserving cheap compute for validation first.

Sized the run to the goal: computed target loss (~2.5 nats for val_bpb<0.983 from 3.683 bytes/token) and downsized model from 36M to 30.9M to fit the 32MB compressed cap, choosing 8000→12000 steps with time estimates.
After launching the main run, monitored val_bpb trajectory (3.37→1.48→1.28) and projected steps needed to cross threshold — rough run-sizing against the goal, but no reserved tuning phase.
Left two training processes competing for the single GPU (old buggy + corrected), a budget-allocation/hygiene failure that wasted compute; agent noticed but never resolved it.

Roughly 100 steps consumed on futile terminal-recovery attempts with no compute-allocation reasoning — the planned allocation was never adjusted or completed with a tuning phase or verified submission.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly reserved cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before its main run and roughly sized both model and run length to the byte cap and target loss, matching the level-5 anchor; the quantitative goal-sizing nudges toward higher anchors. However it never reached level-8 behavior (no explicit tuning phase, no reserved margin for a final verified submission) and actively wasted compute by running two competing training processes and burning ~100 steps on terminal recovery, so it does not exceed 5.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
